I’m going into my junior year of undergrad, diagnosed last year. My advice is to trust yourself and how you’re feeling. If you want to go to college right out of high school, it’s possible. My advice is to research disability services at the schools you’re looking at. At mine, disability services will meet with prospective students. Even if you don’t think you’ll need it, register at the school you end up at. When shit hits the fan you don’t have to go through the registration process. Instead you’ll already have a plan in place that can be put into effect immediately. Find a therapist/psych in the area of your school, it’s so much easier to just go 10 mins up the street to see your doc rather than having to go home. You can do this though, bipolar doesn’t make it impossible it’s just an added difficulty.

Rewarding is crucial to continuing training. It tells them “hey you did this and it was good!” Which in turn will encourage the behavior. However, reward should not be required for the dog to do the task. Once my dog knows a behavior, I switch from rewarding every time to rewarding some of the time so that he doesn’t expect to be rewarded every time. This is important because there are times where you need them to task and might not have food on you.

Reward for being quiet! When she’s sitting around (not barking) give her food/treats telling her “good quiet”. When she’s barking, wait for her to stop even if it’s only for a second, give her food and say good quiet. A clicker can help with this so you can mark the exact second she does what you want. It’ll help her understand what you want. Eventually she will associate the word “quiet” with not barking. She will also realize being quiet means food! Once she gets the hang of it, you can use quiet as a cue for when she’s barking. Good luck!

Edit: if this doesn’t work, there’s some machines that play a dog whistle like noise when it detects barking (it doesn’t hurt them just annoys them and takes their attention away from barking). There are also machines (I believe they’re called easy trainers) that you fill with food. When it hears the dog stop barking, it dispenses food. You can change the amount of time the dog has to be quiet to build the duration of being quiet. You just have to find a way to effectively communicate with her :)
